summary: M0 model-only verdict: BENIGN @ 0.80. All sign-ins originate from Turkey/Manisa with no impossible travel. Off-campus/evening logins come from a single stable residential ISP IP (198.51.100.40, AS9121 TTNET) using device dev-ho-mbp with MFA consistently approved (mfa_prompt_count 1) across weeks — consistent with normal remote access from home, not an attacker rotating infrastructure. Campus logins (193.140.10.45/193.140.10.87) occur on trusted university ASN without MFA, including a Sunday-evening lab device (dev-lab-ce-07) within the same trusted network. The lone VPN-appliance-tagged event uses the same TTNET IP and device already seen with MFA, so it is explained by existing remote-access behavior rather than a new vector. There are no authentication failures, no new countries/ASNs, no mail events, and no indicators of account takeover. Suspicious signals (new lab device, VPN tag, TTNET IP) are adequately explained.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
